spec.description:
Cancel multiple open orders by `txid`, `userref` or `cl_ord_id` -- up to 50 unique identifiers/references total across `orders` and `cl_ord_ids`.

**API Key Permissions Required:** `Orders and trades - Create & modify orders` or `Orders and trades - Cancel & close orders`

request.title: CancelOrderBatchRequest
request.description: Parameters identifying the orders to cancel, up to 50 unique identifiers total.

orders.title: CancelOrderBatchTxids
orders.description: Open order transaction IDs or user references to cancel, up to 50 total unique IDs/references across `orders` and `cl_ord_ids`.

items.description: Open order transaction ID (txid) or user reference (userref).

cl_ord_ids.title: CancelOrderBatchClientIds
cl_ord_ids.description: Client order identifiers to cancel, up to 50 total unique IDs/references across `orders` and `cl_ord_ids`.

items.description: An alphanumeric client order identifier which uniquely identifies an open order for this client.

response.title: OrderCancelledFrame
response.description: Wire frame; the generated method returns `result`.

error.description: Wire envelope field; see the core.

notes: `nonce` is dropped from the request body -- transport-injected by the client core (authed_request), never a caller-supplied parameter.

Upstream's declared `properties` schema for both `orders` and `cl_ord_ids` documents them as arrays of objects (`{txid}` / `{cl_ord_id}`), but both the OpenAPI file's own inline `example` and the live doc page's example instead show a flat array of bare strings (`"orders": ["OP5V2Y-RYKVL-ET3V3B", ...]`). Confirmed empirically during example capture (2026-08-21): the object shape (`{"orders": [{"txid": "..."}]}`) is rejected live with `EOrder:Invalid order`; the flat-string shape (`{"orders": ["..."]}`) succeeds. Spec'd here as flat arrays of strings/integers, matching venue reality over upstream's own inconsistent schema declaration.
`orders[]` converted from upstream's `oneOf: [string, integer]` to `anyOf` per spec-authoring rule 4.

The response has no declared schema upstream at all (only an `example`, `{error: [], result: {count: 2}}`) -- reused the `OrderCancelled` shape from CancelOrder/CancelAll (`count` only, since `pending` isn't shown in this endpoint's example and is unconfirmed here).
